page.layout: One page of running text in a single column below the running head "EPISTOLA"; a marginal note in the left margin beside the line "Inde enim"; a catchword at the lower right. No page number is printed.

main_text.p: per argumentis transfixit: vix ut Mihi (post tam illustres pugiles) quicquam negotij superfit, nisi, quùm Sacerdotes prætextu quodam Spiritualitatis evehendos, & Principes. Ipsorum humilitatis obtentu deprimendos esse docuerit, ut Ego larvam, hanc Illi detrahaṁ[?], quo vulnus Eius Principibus baudquaquam benignus appareat: ac deindè Eum, in hac Causa, erroris convincam, ex ipsis Sociorum suorum confessionibus, imò suis. Quos non parum torqueri certum est, quoties sentiunt se (quod genus pugnæ exhorruisse dicitur Lulianus) pœnis[?] proprijs vulnerari. Inde Maldon. in expos. unius Scripturæ Ioh.6.53.enim est, quòd alicubi Maldonatus Iesuita fateri cogatur, Se impeditum esse, quo minùs acriter & vehementer in Protestantes invehatur, quia Catholici quidam ijs se junxerant.

p.i: Hasce qualescunque lucubratiunculas Tibi potissimùm (inclytissime Princeps) consecrare causæ plurimæ me impulerunt. Bellarminus Librum, quo Principum

page.notes: The left-margin note is set in very small type; I read it as "Maldon. in expos. unius Scripturæ" with "Ioh.6.53." beneath. The first letters are partly obscured, so "Maldon." may be an abbreviation of Maldonatus. "detrahaṁ[?]" is uncertain: the word may be "detraham" or "detrahat". "pœnis[?]" is uncertain at this resolution. Italic and roman type is distinguished by eye and is approximate; proper names and some words I took as roman. The faint "Digitized by Google" mark in the lower right corner is excluded as a digitiser's mark.
